requirement:
The coverage index MUST present a file coverage map of all current first-party
Rust files under {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` as its
primary overview. Its counts MUST use only the records eligible for the
combined view under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, following
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map`.

The overview MUST visibly identify coverage excluded because it is stale,
missing, or unreadable. When those exclusions leave no usable selected
records, the map MUST show coverage as unavailable; when no coverage has been
recorded, files MUST show "not measured" and the collection guidance of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.unavailable` MUST remain visible.
The test and run details required by
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary` MUST remain available on
demand rather than expanded by default.
rationale:
The three marked tests in `src/execution_coverage/book.rs` cover every obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.combined`. I did not open `map_html` or `file_card`; I took their names to mean they pull out the map HTML and a single file's card.

- **All current first-party Rust files on the map.** `fn[file_maps_union_process_locations_and_filter_unexecuted_test_files]` lists `code.rs`, `zero.rs` and `unmeasured.rs`. `fn[maps_distinguish_no_runs_zero_hits_stale_and_incomplete_coverage]` checks that a newly added `new.rs` appears on the map.
- **Counts use only eligible records.**
  - The first test asserts the union total "2/4 (50.0%)" across the test and child process, and "2/3 … 66.7%" for `code.rs`.
  - `fn[incomplete_attempts_do_not_label_their_files_as_unmeasured_in_a_partial_map]` has a good attempt and a bad one. `code.rs` is 100.0% from the good attempt alone, so the unavailable attempt and later the stale attempt add nothing to the counts.
- **Visible identification of excluded coverage.** The tests assert the index text "1 stale test attempts", "1 unavailable test attempts" and "Coverage history is incomplete". These cover stale sources or inputs, a removed or missing profile, and unreadable `attempt.json`.
- **Unavailable when exclusions leave nothing usable.** The stale case shows `code.rs` and `new.rs` as "unavailable" with no `%`. The unreadable and missing-profile cases do the same. The partial-map test shows the affected `other.rs` as "unavailable" and not "not measured".
- **No coverage recorded.** The no-runs case asserts that the `code.rs` card says "not measured" and that the index contains "Run `habeas coverage`".
- **Details on demand.** The rendered HTML contains `<details class="habeas-coverage-details">` without `open`. The detail page's `Run and attempt details` section is not open by default and comes after the map.
- **Zero and not-measured distinctions.** `zero.rs` shows "0.0%", and `unmeasured.rs` shows "not measured" with no `%`.

The "other configurations are excluded historical coverage" obligation belongs to `requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`, which this requirement only cites. The assertions are mostly substring checks, but they pin the specific required outcomes. I found no scenario that the tests would accept in violation of the text. There are no acknowledgments to consider.

text: :::{req} index.file_map.combined
The coverage index MUST present a file coverage map of all current first-party
Rust files under {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` as its
primary overview. Its counts MUST use only the records eligible for the
combined view under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, following
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map`.
The overview MUST visibly identify coverage excluded because it is stale,
missing, or unreadable. When those exclusions leave no usable selected
records, the map MUST show coverage as unavailable; when no coverage has been
recorded, files MUST show "not measured" and the collection guidance of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.unavailable` MUST remain visible.
The test and run details required by
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary` MUST remain available on
demand rather than expanded by default.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Search results are not evidence inputs under {cite}`requirements.authoring.text_search`, so only sources an assessment received as mandatory inputs or read count. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
:::{req} index.selection
The coverage index MUST combine the most recent recorded test attempt for each
nextest binary and test name among the retained runs. "Most recent" MUST refer
to when the attempt started, including failed or interrupted attempts. A newer
filtered run MUST update only the tests it executes, leaving other compatible
test records available to the combined view. A newer attempt with missing or
unreadable coverage MUST be shown as unavailable rather than replaced with an
older successful attempt. Results from incompatible instrumented build
configurations MUST NOT be combined under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration`.
The main combined view MUST use the instrumented build configuration of the
most recently started recorded test attempt. Latest-per-test selection MUST
occur within that configuration. Records from other configurations MUST be
identified as excluded historical coverage. Configuration selection MUST use
recorded metadata without building or executing tests.
:::{req} index.freshness
Only records whose captured source inputs match the current project source and
whose build configurations are compatible MAY contribute execution counts to
the combined view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`.
Records invalidated by a source change, or whose compatibility cannot be
established, MUST be identified as stale or unavailable and excluded from the
combined coverage totals. Their retained per-process reports MUST remain
inspectable using their captured source until the build artifacts are removed.
:::{req} index.file_map
A file coverage map MUST identify each file by its workspace-relative path and
show its covered and instrumented line counts and percentage. These counts MUST
use the union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`,
restricted to the file and the records represented by that map, including
associated child processes. The map MUST visually distinguish coverage levels
while also displaying percentages as text. The percentage MUST describe the
map's recorded instrumented lines, rather than all physical source lines.
A listed file with instrumented lines but no positive execution counts MUST
show 0%. A listed file with no recorded instrumented lines in otherwise usable
coverage MUST show "not measured" without a percentage. Coverage whose
completeness cannot be established MUST be identified as unavailable rather
than as 0% or "not measured".
:::{req} index.unavailable
When no coverage run has been recorded, the coverage index MUST show a readable
message explaining how to collect one. Missing, unreadable, or incomplete run
data MUST produce a visible diagnostic in the index or affected process report
without preventing the rest of the book from rendering.
:::{req} index.summary
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST identify the
contributing runs and show each selected test's binary, test name, attempt,
capture time, command, selection, and outcome, including missing or stale
coverage. It MUST show source revisions and uncommitted-source state when
available rather than present records from several runs as one run.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST link to {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.details`, visibly identify
incomplete coverage, and MUST NOT imply that every current test has coverage
merely because all available records are valid.
